en: Jātaka: The Second Book of Birth Stories (Dukanipāta), Chapter on the Firm (Daḷhavagga)
9. The Mora Jātaka:
“Rising as the sole king, the one with eyes, the color of a harissa flower, the radiance of the earth;”
I pay homage to that one, the color of a lotus, who illuminates the earth;
protected by him, may we dwell safely this day.
Those brahmins who have mastered all things, the knowers of the Vedas...
To them I bow, and may they protect me.
Homage to the Buddhas, homage to Awakening!
Homage to the liberated ones, homage to Liberation!
Having made this protection,
that peacock wanders in search [of food].
This one-eyed king has departed.
Golden-hued, radiant as the earth;
I pay homage to you, golden-hued and radiant as the earth,
so that we may dwell protected by you tonight.
To those brahmins who have mastered the Vedas and all phenomena, to them I pay homage, and may they protect me.
Homage be to the Buddhas; homage be to Awakening.
"Homage to those who are liberated, homage to liberation!
Having made this protective chant,
the peacock established his dwelling."
The Morajātakam, the ninth.
